doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Writing by hand and the need for a home studio
summary: She sketches on a notepad and uses the computer only for large ensemble scores; compares Dave Rivello's workspace and her Montreal studio.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you write at the computer?

No. I wish. I can barely turn my computer on when I’m composing. Once I get into it I will, and that means writing larger ensemble music. I can write all small sketches on a notepad. That’s what I do. Yeah.
Okay. I remember going to the house of your colleague Dave Rivello and I was pleased to see this big — it was almost like an architectural type table and he had his King manuscript paper.

He’s very good at outlining with all that. I wish I was as organized. Although I mean every artist has their space, I think there’s been lots of documentaries on that. But your living/sort of working space and it’s certainly — I actually thought oh I’m finally going to be a real professor with my own office at a school and I’m going to work there. And I can barely work there because there’s too much work there. I still need my own space to work in. So your home space becomes really important I think once you figure that out.

And Dave’s done a great job of that with having lots of space to freely write. And that’s kind of what I have with my studio in Montreal that I’m still spending a lot of time at, and hopefully I’ll develop one here more but I haven’t yet because I’m still trying to figure out Rochester.
